data.title: SQLite = secondary backend, StateStore = primary
data.context: Reflection analysis revealed SQLitePersistence is only used by agentic_db tool, while StateStore remains the primary persistence layer using JSON files. This is clean separation: StateStore handles fast key-value persistence (decisions, TODOs, reflections, RAG, skills, episodes) via JSON files, while SQLite handles structured queries and advanced data access via agentic_db tool. Both coexist without conflict. No need to wire SQLite into StateStore — two backends, one purpose.
data.alternatives: 1) Wire SQLite as StateStore backend — adds complexity, dependency on better-sqlite3, unnecessary for key-value workloads. 2) Replace StateStore entirely with SQLite — breaks backward compatibility, adds maintenance burden.
data.consequence: Clear architecture: StateStore (JSON) for simple persistence, SQLite (agentic_db) for complex queries. Developers know exactly where to store what.
